title: β-Lactamase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Shows Dynamics in the Active Site That Increase upon Inhibitor Binding.
experiment: 15N T1, T2, and 15N-{1H} NOE spin relaxation with anisotropic Lipari-Szabo model-free analysis at 600 MHz (14 T) and 850 MHz (20 T)
construct_or_mutation: wild-type BlaC without signal peptide and TEV-cleaved N-terminal 6xHis tag (construct residues 1-266 = G1 plus UniProt P9WKD3-1 residues 43-307; Ambler numbering used in text)
other_conditions: 0.38 mM 15N-enriched BlaC; tumbling: tau_c = 13.81 ± 0.04 ns (HydroNMR from 5NJ2: 14.5 ns); average S2 > 0.9; average T1 = 1.7 s and average T2 = 45 ms at 20 T; V80 fitted with Model 5 (S2 = 0.57 ± 0.02, Sf2 = 0.79 ± 0.03); 仅图示 for other loop S2 and Models 3/4 Rex residues (Fig. S2-S4)
author_claim: Resting-state BlaC is overall highly rigid on the ps-ns timescale (average S2 > 0.9), with only Val80 at the helix 2/helix 7 interface exhibiting significant fast internal motion (S2 = 0.57 ± 0.02, Sf2 = 0.79 ± 0.03) and minor flexibility in surface loops.
anchor: Model 5, including an extra local-order parameter Sf2 for very fast motion, was used to ﬁt only the data for Val80. The resulting order parameters are Sf2 ⫽ 0.79 ⫾ 0.03 and S2 ⫽ 0.57 ⫾ 0.02, the latter of which is the lowest order parameter in the protein.
locator: Results, Resting-state BlaC, p. 4; 仅图示: supp_PMC7038250_AAC.02025-19-s0001.pdf Fig. S2-S4; conditions: Materials and Methods, p. 10 and Fig. S11
caveat_note: BMRB 27888 is this paper's free-state deposit matching 298 K, pH 6.4, 94 mM MES, 6% D2O, and 600/850 MHz; the deposit card sample string lists the 0.7 mM [U-13C; U-15N] assignment sample, whereas Methods states spin relaxation was recorded on 0.38 mM 15N-enriched BlaC. Authors use Ambler beta-lactamase numbering throughout (mapping to construct residues 1-266 is in supp_PMC7038250_AAC.02025-19-s0001.pdf Fig. S11). Refutes Sagar et al. (ref. 41) SAXS open-state proposal for apo BlaC because experimental tau_c (13.81 ± 0.04 ns) matches closed crystal structure 5NJ2 (14.5 ns).

title: β-Lactamase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Shows Dynamics in the Active Site That Increase upon Inhibitor Binding.
experiment: 1H-15N TROSY-HSQC line broadening and missing active-site resonances at 600 MHz (14 T) and 850 MHz (20 T)
construct_or_mutation: wild-type BlaC without signal peptide and TEV-cleaved N-terminal 6xHis tag (construct residues 1-266 = G1 plus UniProt P9WKD3-1 residues 43-307; Ambler numbering used in text)
other_conditions: 0.7 mM 15N-13C-enriched BlaC (assignment) / 0.38 mM 15N-enriched BlaC; regime (authors): intermediate to fast exchange process may be present in the active site; inferred delta-delta > 0.1 ppm (1H) and/or > 1 ppm (15N) at 20 T; 仅图示 for surrounding lowered-intensity amides (Fig. 2a)
population: minor state >15% (Bloch-McConnell lower bound from broadening beyond detection at 20 T at 860 s-1)
author_claim: Four conserved active-site residues (Ser70, Ser130, Thr235, Thr237) are broadened beyond detection and surrounding amides show reduced peak intensity in resting-state BlaC, requiring a minor-state population >15% under Bloch-McConnell exchange at 860 s^-1 at 20 T.
anchor: On the basis of the Bloch-McConnell equations for chemical exchange, it can be shown that at an exchange rate of 860 s⫺1, the population of the minor state must be sizeable (⬎15%) for the resonances of Ser70, Ser130, Thr235, and Thr237 to broaden beyond detection at 20 T.
locator: Discussion, p. 7; Results, Resting-state BlaC, p. 3 and Fig. 2a (仅图示); conditions: Materials and Methods, p. 10
caveat_note: The >15% minor-state population is not directly fitted from CPMG dispersion (where population could not be determined accurately) but deduced via Bloch-McConnell equations from complete broadening of S70, S130, T235, and T237 at 20 T assuming they share the 860 s^-1 exchange rate. Phosphate titration in prior work (ref. 31) did not restore these peaks, ruling out buffer ion exchange.

title: β-Lactamase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Shows Dynamics in the Active Site That Increase upon Inhibitor Binding.
experiment: 15N TROSY-CPMG relaxation dispersion at 600 MHz (14 T) and 850 MHz (20 T)
construct_or_mutation: wild-type BlaC without signal peptide and TEV-cleaved N-terminal 6xHis tag (construct residues 1-266 = G1 plus UniProt P9WKD3-1 residues 43-307; Ambler numbering used in text)
other_conditions: 1.0 mM (at 20 T) or 0.8 mM (at 14 T) 15N-enriched BlaC; T_ex = 40 ms; nu_CPMG = 25 to 1,000 s-1; 仅图示 (8 active-site residues in group fit and Rex > 3 s-1 spheres plotted only in Fig. 3a,c, Fig. 4, and Fig. S5)
timescale: kex = (8.6 ± 0.6) × 10^2 s^-1; ca. 860 s^-1 (global two-state fit over 8 active-site residues)
author_claim: Resting-state BlaC exhibits low-millisecond conformational exchange localized around the active site with kex = (8.6 ± 0.6) × 10^2 s^-1, faster than the maximum catalytic turnover rate (kcat = 111 ± 4 s^-1 for nitrocefin) and consistent with omega-loop motion.
anchor: Eight active-site residues that showed similar dispersion proﬁles at both magnetic ﬁeld strengths were used in a group ﬁt (Fig. 4 and Fig. S5), yielding a chemical exchange rate of (8.6 ⫾ 0.6) ⫻ 102 s⫺1.
locator: Results, Resting-state BlaC, p. 4; 仅图示: Fig. 3a,c, Fig. 4, and supp_PMC7038250_AAC.02025-19-s0001.pdf Fig. S5; conditions: Materials and Methods, p. 10-11
caveat_note: Same buffer, pH 6.4, 298 K, and 600/850 MHz fields as BMRB 27888, but CPMG was recorded on 1.0 mM (20 T) and 0.8 mM (14 T) 15N-enriched BlaC rather than the 0.7 mM 13C/15N sample listed on the deposit card. Excited-state population and delta-omega could not be determined accurately from CPMG alone. Individual identities of the 8 globally fitted residues are only inside Fig. 4 and Fig. S5 graphics.

title: β-Lactamase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Shows Dynamics in the Active Site That Increase upon Inhibitor Binding.
experiment: 15N CEST saturation transfer (B1 = 8 Hz and 25 Hz)
construct_or_mutation: wild-type BlaC without signal peptide and TEV-cleaved N-terminal 6xHis tag (construct residues 1-266 = G1 plus UniProt P9WKD3-1 residues 43-307; Ambler numbering used in text)
other_conditions: 0.8 mM [15N]BlaC; 0.8-s B1 irradiation at 8 and 25 Hz over 100.5 to 130 ppm (0.5 ppm step); CEST detection window 20 to 200 s-1; example flat curve shown for E166 in Fig. S6
author_claim: 15N CEST at 298 K with 8 Hz and 25 Hz saturation fields shows no secondary dips for any residue, indicating no significant slow exchange in the 20 to 200 s^-1 window in resting-state BlaC.
anchor: saturation ﬁelds of 25 Hz and 8 Hz and at temperatures of 298 K and 288 K all failed to reveal chemical exchange for any of the residues, suggesting that no signiﬁcant dynamics in the CEST timescale of 20 to 200 s⫺1 are present.
locator: Results, Resting-state BlaC, p. 4-5; supp_PMC7038250_AAC.02025-19-s0001.pdf Fig. S6; conditions: Materials and Methods, p. 10-11
caveat_note: Same buffer, pH 6.4, and 298 K as BMRB 27888, but measured on 0.8 mM [15N]BlaC (vs 0.7 mM 13C/15N on deposit card), and Methods does not specify whether 600 MHz or 850 MHz was used for CEST. Glu166 (E166) is named only in supp_PMC7038250_AAC.02025-19-s0001.pdf Fig. S6 as an example non-exchanging residue.

title: β-Lactamase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Shows Dynamics in the Active Site That Increase upon Inhibitor Binding.
experiment: 1H-15N TROSY-HSQC line broadening upon avibactam binding at 850 MHz (20 T)
construct_or_mutation: wild-type BlaC without signal peptide and TEV-cleaved N-terminal 6xHis tag (construct residues 1-266 = G1 plus UniProt P9WKD3-1 residues 43-307; Ambler numbering used in text)
other_conditions: 0.38 mM 15N-enriched BlaC + 2 mM avibactam (assignment: 0.3 mM 15N-13C-enriched BlaC + 2 mM avibactam, BMRB 27929); TITAN lineshape titration (0-0.9 mM avibactam on C69, R161, L162, E168, Y241, A274) gives upper limits KD <= 10 uM and koff <= 10 s-1 (best fit KD = 0.14 uM, koff = 2.4 s-1 in Fig. S7; slow binding exchange <<100 s-1); 仅图示 for broadened active-site residues (Fig. 2a,c and Fig. 3d)
alt_state_structure: 6H2H: avibactam-bound BlaC with slightly open Ω-loop conformation (Discussion, p. 8; Fig. 6)
author_claim: Avibactam binding broadens additional active-site backbone amides beyond detection in 1H-15N TROSY-HSQC spectra, demonstrating enhanced active-site chemical exchange inside the bound complex rather than conformational locking.
anchor: Interestingly, several peaks that are visible in the spectrum of resting-state BlaC broaden beyond detection upon binding with avibactam (Fig. 2). These peaks correspond to amides around the binding site, indicating that inhibitor binding induces enhanced chemical exchange broadening in the active site.
locator: Results, Avibactam, p. 5; 仅图示: Fig. 2a,c and Fig. 3d; titration: Materials and Methods, p. 11 and supp_PMC7038250_AAC.02025-19-s0001.pdf Fig. S7
caveat_note: Sample contains 2 mM avibactam (deposited separately as BMRB 27929; BMRB 27888 is apo BlaC). If the broadening beyond detection at 20 T is driven by the ~3,400 s^-1 CPMG process, delta-delta > ca. 0.3 ppm (1H) and/or 3 ppm (15N) or multiple exchange processes are required.

title: β-Lactamase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Shows Dynamics in the Active Site That Increase upon Inhibitor Binding.
experiment: 1H-15N TROSY-HSQC line broadening and slow-exchange peak splitting at 850 MHz (20 T)
ligand_or_partner: clavulanic acid (100 mM initial; covalent 70-Da adduct)
construct_or_mutation: wild-type BlaC without signal peptide and TEV-cleaved N-terminal 6xHis tag (construct residues 1-266 = G1 plus UniProt P9WKD3-1 residues 43-307; Ambler numbering used in text)
other_conditions: 0.38 mM 15N-enriched BlaC + 100 mM clavulanic acid (assignment: 0.4 mM 15N-13C-enriched BlaC + 186 mM clavulanic acid, BMRB 27890; ~1.2-h turnover keeps covalent 70-Da adduct near 100%); at least 21 resonances split into >=2 peaks around active site and alpha domain; 仅图示 (mapped on structure in Fig. 2a,b and Fig. 5)
alt_state_structure: 5A92: bound BlaC showing alternate Lys73 side-chain orientation (Discussion, p. 8-9; Fig. 7); 5A91: unbound BlaC showing canonical Lys73 side-chain orientation (Discussion, p. 8-9; Fig. 7)
author_claim: Formation of the 70-Da covalent clavulanic acid adduct broadens active-site amides beyond detection and splits at least 21 resonances in the active site and alpha domain into doubled peaks (relative occupancy 42% ± 3%), revealing an additional slower exchange process (kex < 100 s^-1) potentially linked to Lys73 side-chain reorientation.
anchor: The occupancies of the observed states, 41 and 59%, respectively, also match the relative occupancies of the doubled peaks of 42% ⫾ 3% that we observed in our clavulanic acid adduct-bound-state spectra.
locator: Discussion, p. 8; Abstract, p. 1 (kex < 100 s-1); Results, Clavulanic acid, p. 6; 仅图示: Fig. 2a,b and Fig. 5; conditions: Materials and Methods, p. 10
caveat_note: Clavulanic acid adduct sample (deposited separately as BMRB 27890; BMRB 27888 is apo BlaC). Over days, broad background signal appears in the spectral center suggesting gradual molten-globule formation; noncovalent binding of a second clavulanate molecule cannot be completely excluded at 100 mM, though S70A control in ref. 38 showed no line broadening.

title: β-Lactamase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Shows Dynamics in the Active Site That Increase upon Inhibitor Binding.
experiment: 15N T1, T2, and 15N-{1H} NOE spin relaxation at 850 MHz (20 T)
ligand_or_partner: clavulanic acid (100 mM initial; covalent 70-Da adduct)
construct_or_mutation: wild-type BlaC without signal peptide and TEV-cleaved N-terminal 6xHis tag (construct residues 1-266 = G1 plus UniProt P9WKD3-1 residues 43-307; Ambler numbering used in text)
other_conditions: 0.38 mM 15N-enriched BlaC + 100 mM clavulanic acid; average T1 = 1.8 s and average T2 = 40 ms (vs 1.7 s and 45 ms in free BlaC, attributed to viscosity of 100 mM clavulanic acid); elevated T2 > 60 ms and lower NOE (< 0.75) in loops, termini, and 6 residues at helices 2/7 hydrophobic interface; 仅图示 (Fig. 5, Fig. S8, and Fig. S9)
author_claim: Clavulanic acid adduct formation induces elevated T2 (>60 ms) and reduced 15N-{1H} NOE in loops, termini, and six residues at the hydrophobic packing interface between helices 2 and 7, indicating local loss of ps-ns rigidity in the alpha domain.
anchor: Strikingly higher transverse relaxation times were found for several residues in and near loops and terminal regions, as well as for six residues involved in the hydrophobic packing interface between helices 2 and 7 in the ␣ subunit.
locator: Results, Clavulanic acid, p. 6; 仅图示: Fig. 5 and supp_PMC7038250_AAC.02025-19-s0001.pdf Fig. S8-S9; conditions: Materials and Methods, p. 10
caveat_note: Clavulanic acid adduct sample (BMRB 27890) measured at single field (850 MHz / 20 T), whereas BMRB 27888 is apo BlaC. Gradual molten-globule background signal develops over days, and higher global T1/lower average T2 reflect increased viscosity from 100 mM clavulanic acid.

title: β-Lactamase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Shows Dynamics in the Active Site That Increase upon Inhibitor Binding.
experiment: 15N TROSY-CPMG relaxation dispersion at 850 MHz (20 T)
ligand_or_partner: clavulanic acid (100 mM initial; covalent 70-Da adduct)
construct_or_mutation: wild-type BlaC without signal peptide and TEV-cleaved N-terminal 6xHis tag (construct residues 1-266 = G1 plus UniProt P9WKD3-1 residues 43-307; Ambler numbering used in text)

author_claim: In clavulanate-bound BlaC, active-site resonances broadened in free BlaC disappear completely while Glu168, Asp273, and residues near the Ile105 loop and omega-loop base retain ms CPMG dispersion similar to resting-state BlaC.
anchor: Residues Glu168 and Asp273 were found to have dispersion proﬁles with shapes similar to those in the active-site exchange of the resting-state protein (e.g., Fig. 4b).
locator: Results, Clavulanic acid, p. 6; 仅图示: Fig. 3a,b and Fig. 4; conditions: Materials and Methods, p. 10-11

Peak splitting, active-site broadening beyond detection, gradual molten-globule background, and technical noise (29/208 profiles excluded) prevented fitting a global kex.

title: β-Lactamase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Shows Dynamics in the Active Site That Increase upon Inhibitor Binding.
experiment: Crystal structure comparison of free, avibactam-bound, clavulanic-acid-bound, and XFEL ceftriaxone-reaction BlaC structures
ligand_or_partner: free, avibactam, clavulanic acid adduct, and ceftriaxone catalytic reaction snapshots
construct_or_mutation: Mycobacterium tuberculosis BlaC crystal structures (Ambler numbering)
other_conditions: C-alpha atoms of N170 and R171 positioned ~2 Å further from active site in 6H2H; XFEL snapshots at 30, 100, 500, and 2,000 ms from Olmos et al. (ref. 42) show alternative K73 and S130 side-chain orientations
population: 41% and 59% (crystallographic occupancies of the two Lys73/Ser130 conformations reported by Olmos et al., ref. 42)
alt_state_structure: 6H2H: avibactam-bound BlaC with slightly open Ω-loop conformation (Discussion, p. 8; Fig. 6); 5A92: bound BlaC showing alternate Lys73 side-chain orientation (Discussion, p. 8-9; Fig. 7); 5A91: unbound BlaC showing canonical Lys73 side-chain orientation (Discussion, p. 8-9; Fig. 7)
author_claim: Comparison of BlaC crystal structures identifies a ~2 Å outward omega-loop displacement at Asn170/Arg171 in avibactam-bound PDB 6H2H and two Lys73/Ser130 conformations (41% and 59% occupancies in XFEL structures 5A91/5A92) as candidate structural models for the NMR active-site exchange processes.
anchor: In the structure of PDB code 6H2H (38) BlaC bound to avibactam, however, the ⍀ loop was observed in a slightly open conformation, with the C␣ atoms of Asn170 and Arg171 positioned ⬃2 Å further away from the active site than their canonical positions, providing further support for the model of ⍀-loop movement (Fig. 6).
caveat_note: Reanalysis/comparison of previously published crystal and XFEL structures (refs. 31, 34, 38, 42, 61) rather than new crystallography in this paper; 41% and 59% occupancies come from Olmos et al. (ref. 42) XFEL structures of ceftriaxone hydrolysis.
